name: Perimeter Block
summary: Buildings line all four edges of the block, creating a continuous street wall and a private interior. Eixample is the canonical example. Typical FAR 1.5-3.5.

name: Courtyard Block
summary: Perimeter block with a generous internal courtyard for daylight and amenity. Berlin Mietshaus, Vienna Hof. Typical FAR 2.0-4.0.

name: Tower on Podium
summary: Slender tower(s) rising from a low active podium. Common in Hong Kong, Vancouver, Singapore. Typical FAR 4.0-12.

name: Row House
summary: Single-family attached dwellings sharing party walls; 3-5 stories. Brownstone, Georgian terrace. Typical density 60-150 DU/ha.

name: Superblock
summary: Multiple traditional blocks aggregated into pedestrian-priority cells with through-traffic restricted to perimeter arterials. Barcelona Superilla; Chinese danwei.

name: Transect T1 — Natural
summary: Lands unsuitable for or protected from settlement: wetlands, steep slopes, watersheds. Within New Urbanism transect.

name: Transect T3 — Sub-Urban
summary: Low-density residential areas adjacent to higher zones. Single-family, deep setbacks, FAR ~0.3-0.5.

name: Transect T5 — Urban Center
summary: Higher-density mixed-use building types accommodating retail, offices, rowhouses, apartments. FAR 2.0-4.0.

name: Transect T6 — Urban Core
summary: Highest-density and -intensity zone with the greatest variety of uses. Civic buildings, regional commerce, towers. FAR 4.0+.

name: Complete Street
summary: Right-of-way designed for all users. Sidewalks, cycle facilities, transit, traffic-calmed motor vehicle lanes, street trees.

name: Woonerf
summary: Dutch shared street where pedestrians have priority and cars travel at walking pace. Curbless, mixed surface, scattered planting.

name: Linear Park
summary: Long, thin park form connecting destinations and serving multiple neighbourhoods. Often retrofit on disused infrastructure.
